sketches.title: Once Upon a Quick Stop
sketches.premise: The Host gives you a boring weekday errand and a fairy-tale opening. Turn the errand into the first paragraph of a story, while keeping the errand’s two ordinary things real. Make it magical, rude, romantic, or gloriously doomed; just don’t lose the shopping.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the move remains a fairy-tale opening and that both named errand nouns still exist in the situation and keep their stated roles.
sketches.move_shape: Write one or two story-opening sentences, under 90 characters, containing the card’s two nouns and its opening cue. Example: “At the laundromat, brave Ella sought a sock and faced the dragon dryer.”
sketches.first_card: Opening: “In a kingdom before lunch…” Errand: return a library book and buy toothpaste.

sketches.title: The Quest Is Calling
sketches.premise: You are stuck on hold during a weekday errand. The Host gives you a fairy-tale quest and two plain nouns; answer as the caller, making one short spoken line. The quest must still be underway, but your excuse can be noble, filthy, tragic, or obviously bullshit.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the line sounds spoken on a call, keeps the quest’s goal and obstacle intact, and includes the two card nouns in usable roles.
sketches.move_shape: Give one caller line, under 90 characters, with the nouns and the quest intact. Example: “I can’t slay the ogre yet—I’m at the bank with a ticket and a wet sock.”
sketches.first_card: Quest: cross the cursed bridge to deliver a pie; nouns: bus and receipt.

sketches.title: The Enchanted Receipt
sketches.premise: A weekday receipt has been enchanted into a fairy-tale object. The Host gives you two mundane nouns and the object’s true job. Describe its new magical power in one item-card line, keeping that job useful. The Host will lovingly mock anything that sounds like a haunted coupon.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the entry is an item description, preserves the object’s stated everyday function, and gives both nouns a clear place in the enchantment.
sketches.move_shape: Write one item-card sentence, under 90 characters. Example: “A bus pass that summons coaches, but only after showing one rude receipt.”
sketches.first_card: Object: grocery receipt; job: prove what you bought; nouns: onions and moon.

sketches.title: The Path That Should Take Five Minutes
sketches.premise: You begin a tiny weekday errand in a fairy tale, then meet one obstacle. Answer with the next beat: a choice, bargain, or action that moves the errand forward. Keep the two plain nouns in play, because apparently buying batteries requires defeating a goblin now.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the move is a next story beat, keeps the errand’s destination and obstacle true, and uses both nouns as active parts of the choice or action.
sketches.move_shape: Write one next-beat sentence, under 90 characters, naming the choice or action. Example: “She bribed the troll with a muffin and carried the batteries onward.”
sketches.first_card: Errand: pick up a prescription; obstacle: a sleeping giant blocks the pharmacy; nouns: key and umbrella.

sketches.title: The Castle Customer Complaint
sketches.premise: Your ordinary errand has gone fairy-tale wrong, so file a complaint to the royal service desk. State what happened and what fix you want, while keeping the card’s two nouns and the actual errand’s problem. Petty is encouraged; treason is optional.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the entry is a complaint, preserves the supplied failure as true, and gives a believable requested fix involving both nouns.
sketches.move_shape: Write one complaint, under 90 characters, with the failure and requested fix. Example: “The knight lost my key; refund the toll and return my umbrella.”
sketches.first_card: Errand problem: the laundromat lost one sock; nouns: token and cape; requested fix: replacement.

sketches.title: Leave a Message for the Fairy Godmother
sketches.premise: You have one voicemail to explain why a weekday errand is not finished. Speak as if a fairy godmother is waiting for the update, keeping the card’s two nouns and the real reason you are delayed. You may sound heroic, horny, or like a goblin with a calendar.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the entry is a voicemail update, keeps the stated delay and errand true, and uses both nouns without turning the message into a question or commentary.
sketches.move_shape: Leave one voicemail sentence, under 90 characters. Example: “Hi, I’m late buying bread—the spellbook ate my map, and the bus fled.”
sketches.first_card: Errand: collect a parcel; delay: the shop is closed; nouns: bell and cloak.
